correctness.rationale: For all k>=2, 1<=s<=k and n>=2k+s-1, the graph-state character sum gives an exact flat Schmidt spectrum controlled by a finite-field Kneser cut matrix. Column complementation identifies all cut row types with simultaneous inclusion matrices W_{k-j,m-k}; Ghorbani et al. provide an integral chain basis with modular coefficients C(m-k-i,k-j-i) and block multiplicity C(m,i)-C(m,i-1). Their independent blocks prove the rank sum exactly in every prime. For i=k-s-1, Lucas digit tests for coefficients C(n-2k+1,u), 1<=u<=s, give the exact least-prime-power congruence, and telescoping lower block multiplicities prove both finite error bounds. The standalone checker compares 135 actual finite-field cut ranks, four quantum spectra and 4284 finite resonance instances; those finite checks are not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Marked-point-star cuts of highly symmetric Kneser graph states are a canonical and physically meaningful family of quantum bipartitions. The result gives their complete Schmidt spectra in all prime local dimensions, identifies a sharp congruence gate that activates the first missing incidence block, and establishes distinct polynomial-order behaviors on resonant and nonresonant circumferences. These consequences are structural and extend beyond isolated finite rank computations or trivial normalization checks.
